owner: CC builds; Akien owns the filename's spelling
children: none, because the census says leaf rather than the wish saying so, and the census is the reason the two halves are ONE ticket rather than two. MEASURED 2026-08-19 across the corpus: 37 live emit sites in 18 files (proofs excluded), and the pointer-weight distribution splits them cleanly — bus 32 chars median, charter 29, ground_loop 9, tester 70, trouble 44, and inference_domain 1,171 with a max of 10,078. THE FAT POINTER IS A POPULATION OF ONE, at three call sites in a single module (cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py:319, :373, :408, all passing `pointer=canonical`). So the 'fix the fat pointer' half is not a corpus-wide sweep that would want children — it is three lines and their probe. And the 'file per emission' half has exactly one writer (cairn/tools/base/breadcrumb_log.py, RECORD_NAME + receive_diagnostic) and exactly one reader contract (records(), consumed live only by cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector/inspector.py). THE JOIN THAT MAKES THEM ONE NODE: the filename Akien asked for carries the task, so the file cannot be named until the pointer is short enough to BE a name — a 10,078-character pointer is not a filename on any filesystem here. Splitting them would cast a child whose only falsifier is 'the parent can now proceed', which is a dependency wearing a ticket's clothes. The one thing that looked like a child is NOT mine to spawn and is named rather than folded: the 30-day sweep over the one root is the parent's uncast child (3), the-logs-tree-forgets-after-30-days, and this ticket deliberately stops at making per-record expiry POSSIBLE — it rides out in the bullets to the parent's owner instead.

questions.a: FOUR, and the first is asked to be ratified rather than merely recorded. (1) A PROVED NODE'S FALSIFIER MAY BE RE-SPELLED BY A LATER NODE WITHOUT BEING RETRACTED, provided the later node's own falsifier carries the earlier substance forward explicitly. an-inference-call-logs-that-it-started proved on 2026-08-18 naming diagnostics.jsonl by name and matching trail-to-meter by canonical TEXT; both spellings change here, its record is not edited (Law 7), and clause (5) of this falsifier is where its substance is carried. Without such a rule the corpus either freezes at its first spelling or a proof quietly stops meaning what it proved. I could not find this written anywhere. (2) BUILD-MINIMAL DEFERS THE POLICY; THE CHECK IT DOES NOT PERFORM IS WHETHER THE SHAPE CAN STILL HOLD THE POLICY LATER. This is the general form of the 'WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT' miss, and it is a real addition to build-minimal rather than a criticism of it: deferring rotation was right, and the grain that made rotation inexpressible was chosen in the same breath with nothing asking the question. (3) FILE-PER-EMISSION IS MORE APPEND-ONLY, NOT LESS. It reads like a conflict with breadcrumb_log.py's 'PURE APPEND, ON PURPOSE, AGAINST BOTH PRECEDENTS' and is the opposite: a written file is never reopened at all, where an appended trail is reopened by every later write. (4) A SHAPE THAT CANNOT EXPRESS EXPIRY IS NOT THE SAME AS A SHAPE THAT HAS NOT CHOSEN AN EXPIRY. Easy to lose, and losing it is how the deferral in (2) became invisible.

workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(an_emission_is_one_file_named_by_its_pointer) -> [PROVED] (proved 2026-08-26: 24/24 green, sealed under netns, emission gate clean — probe armed at probes/an_emission_is_one_file_named_by_its_pointer.py; clearance by CC onto cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_emission_gate.py; commit 67d32c9)

watchme.trigger: each firing of the probe over the whole logs tree — it rides the device walk that already exists (ground_loop discovery enumerates class-space device folders, the same walk the parent's probe rides) rather than a clock, and it needs no live host and no inference: both populations it reads are files on disk.
watchme.enough: NOT satisfied by the corpus it was written against, and the reason is that this ticket's failure mode is REGRESSION BY NEW WRITER rather than breakage of the writer it ships. Enough when the invariant has held across at least TWO emitting components that landed AFTER this ticket — each writing one file per emission with a pointer inside the corpus band, without its author having read this ticket — because the thing being watched is whether the grain is carried by the floor or by the discipline of whoever writes the next emit site. A fat pointer is the specific way this decays: it needs no new code and no bad intent, only a caller passing the payload it already has, which is exactly how the one fat pointer in the corpus got there.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier, carrying (a) the count of trail files against the count of records they hold — equal is the invariant, and any file holding two records NAMES that file; (b) the pointer-length distribution per device with the corpus band beside it and every out-of-band device NAMED, because 'the median rose' is a finding nobody can act on and 'inference_domain is at 1,171 against a band of 9-70' is one somebody can open; and (c) the count of surviving diagnostics.jsonl files, which should fall to zero within one retention window and whose failure to fall is itself the finding.
watchme.nexus: the survey tree — this is a census of what the corpus actually writes against what its floor promises, which is the same shape as the parent's coverage measure and belongs in the same memory.
watchme.consumer: cairn/tools/base's owner — the floor owns the record shape, so a device drifting off it is a fact about the floor's reach and not about that device's manners.

intent_berth: none, because this node arose from Akien's direct challenge to a shipped shape on 2026-08-19 rather than from an /intent firing; its durable referents are the sorted berth above and the measurement recorded in `why` (140 emissions, 68 pointers, median inter-emission gap 282s).
dependencies: NONE BLOCKING, and the two that look like dependencies are not. (a) the-logs-tree-forgets-after-30-days (the parent's uncast child (3)) CONSUMES this ticket rather than gating it — this makes per-record expiry expressible and performs no sweep. (b) a-proof-cannot-seed-the-tree-it-reads (sibling child (4), PROVED 2026-08-18) is already landed and is what makes this ticket's clause (3) honest: the join must read rows it did not write, and that discipline exists because of it.
